description: One animation, small enough to be its own metadata. The source IS the post: at 140 graphemes the complete work fits inside a single firehose event, so a client tailing Jetstream can render the piece from the event alone — no index, no appview, no blob fetch, nothing persisted. That is the whole reason the limit is kept rather than raised: a larger record would have to be fetched, fetching needs an index, and an index is the backend this surface exists to do without. `remixOf` makes derivation a first-class backlink, so Constellation answers 'what came from this' for free and the remix tree costs no storage either.

src.description: The program. In `js` it is the body of dwitter's `u(t)`, called at 60fps with `t` in seconds and `S`/`C`/`T`/`R`/`c`/`x` pre-bound over a 1920x1080 canvas that is NOT auto-cleared. In `glsl` it is the body of `main()` in the tweet-shader dialect: `t` seconds, `r` resolution, `FC` fragment coordinate, `o` the out colour. maxLength is the byte guard; maxGraphemes is the limit people actually type against.

lang.description: Which harness runs it. Two hand-golfable languages rather than one fast one: a dweet is read as often as it is run, and compiled output cannot be read, remixed or golfed. `glsl` is where the performance headroom lives — per-pixel on the GPU — without giving up any of that.

title.description: Optional. Dwitter itself has no titles and is not poorer for it; this exists because a remix chain reads better with names in it.

remixOf.description: The dweet this one was golfed from. Set once at birth and never rewritten: it is an attribution edge, not a claim on the parent. The parent's author is not notified by this record's existence — a client that wants that reads the backlink index.
